title: The Resurrection unto Judgment
definition: The doctrine of The Resurrection unto Judgment teaches that those who remain outside of Christ will be raised for judgment, showing that death does not erase accountability before God.
summary: The Resurrection unto Judgment names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. those who remain outside of Christ will be raised for judgment, showing that death does not erase accountability before God. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to The Resurrection unto Judgment because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: those who remain outside of Christ will be raised for judgment, showing that death does not erase accountability before God. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people may treat death as escape if they forget judgment follows it. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let this truth make the Gospel urgent. Pray, witness, and plead with people to come to Christ while mercy is being proclaimed. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
